note: Scripts of tools/hil that do not judge a result and so cannot fail a run: bench utilities that a person runs at the bench (HIL-004). Every other script of the directory either exits non-zero when a check fails or is a library. tools/hil/README.md repeats this list; test_hil_scripts.py keeps the two, and the directory, in agreement.

check_alive.py.purpose: Wake a board's shell with a CR, ask `help`, and print what comes back.
check_alive.py.reason: Shows the shell's answer for a person to read; whether the board is alive is the person's call. It exits 1 only when nothing came back at all.

check_hw.py.purpose: Open the port, wake the shell, ask `help` and print the first bytes of the answer.
check_hw.py.reason: A connection check for a person at the bench; there is no value to compare.

debug_peek.py.purpose: Write the input and output images with `zplc dbg poke` while the board is stopped, then read them back.
debug_peek.py.reason: A probe of what the debug shell lets through: the person reads the replies. It changes memory of a stopped board, so a person runs it.

inspect_zplc.py.purpose: Print the header, segment table and contract draft of a .zplc file.
inspect_zplc.py.reason: Reads a file and prints it; it touches no device and checks nothing against an expectation. It exits 1 only for a file that is not a container.

rescue.py.purpose: Send a break, then `zplc stop` ten times and `zplc reset`, to bring back a board that is stuck.
rescue.py.reason: A recovery action on a board, run by a person; it has no pass or fail.

rescue_device.py.purpose: Send Ctrl+C and Enter five times, then `zplc stop`, and say whether the board answered.
rescue_device.py.reason: A recovery action on a board, run by a person; it has no pass or fail beyond the answer it prints.

sniff.py.purpose: Load a four-byte program, start it in verbose HIL mode and print every line the shell says for five seconds.
sniff.py.reason: A protocol sniffer for a person to read; there is no expected output.
